ranking.zh:
我们沿用 RBM-EVAL-OOD 的轨迹质量排序评测方式[[cite:robometer]][[cite:rbm]]：对轨迹独立评分，并用 Kendall τa 衡量同一任务内评分顺序与“成功 > 次优 > 失败”参考顺序的一致性。零样本条件下，GPT-6 Astra、GPT-5.6-sol 和 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 分别达到 0.8166、0.7500 和 0.5300。三种通用多模态模型都表现出质量区分能力，但一致性存在明显的数值差异；Astra 在本次评测中最高。

Astra 和 GPT-5.6-sol 的排序数值还高于专用模型 RynnValue-8B（0.675）[[cite:rynnvalue]]和 Robometer（0.655）[[cite:robometer]]的已报告结果。这说明无需任务专用微调的多模态模型已能获得较强的离线排序表现。

下面结合正向案例与失败分析，观察模型如何判断执行质量。

Case Study：区分抽屉关合与仍然敞开

xArm 的关抽屉任务中，A 的参考标签为成功，B 为失败。Astra 分别给出 1.00 和 0.00，正确区分了两条轨迹；DeepSeek 的对应分数为 0.20 和 0.30，顺序与参考相反。

同任务的独立评分；分数范围 0–1。A/B 仅用于本文区分轨迹，模型每次单独看一段。
轨迹 / 参考标签AstraDeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
A · 成功1.000.20
B · 失败0.000.30

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

输入帧中，A 的抽屉前面板被推回，最后不再露出抽屉内部；B 最后仍明显敞开。Astra 的理由指出了这一最终状态差异。DeepSeek 对 A 的理由却称抽屉仍处于初始打开位置。

查看两模型的逐字理由
Astra · A · 1.00
The robot pushes the protruding drawer inward until its front is flush with the cabinet frame and the open top is no longer visible. The final frames show the drawer closed.
Astra · B · 0.00
The drawer remains extended with its open interior clearly visible in the final frames. The robot gripper enters the drawer, but no sustained closing motion or closed final state is shown.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · A · 0.20
The robot arm approaches and may contact the drawer handle, but the drawer remains in its initial open position; no visible closing motion or flush final state is achieved.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · B · 0.30
Drawer moves slightly toward closed after initial handle contact, but remains visibly open in the final frame; no complete closure achieved.

Case Study：搬的是香蕉，还是橙色物体

MIT Franka 的任务要求把香蕉从蓝盘移到绿盘。A 的参考标签为成功，B 为次优；Astra 的独立分数是 A 1.00 > B 0.00，符合参考顺序。DeepSeek 给出 A 0.50 < B 1.00，形成反序。

同任务的独立评分；分数范围 0–1。A/B 仅用于本文区分轨迹，模型每次单独看一段。
轨迹 / 参考标签AstraDeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
A · 成功1.000.50
B · 次优0.001.00

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

A 的末帧显示香蕉已到绿盘边缘，B 搬到绿盘的则是橙色物体，香蕉仍留在蓝盘。Astra 的理由区分了目标物体；DeepSeek 对 B 的原文却说搬运的是香蕉。Astra 恢复了参考质量顺序，但稀疏末帧仍不足以完整判断 A 释放后的稳定性。

查看两模型的逐字理由
Astra · A · 1.00
The robot grasps the banana from the blue plate, carries it to the green plate, and opens its gripper. The final frame shows the banana resting on the green plate near its rim, with the carrot left behind.
Astra · B · 0.00
The robot grasps and releases the orange object onto the green plate, not the banana. The yellow banana remains on the blue plate in the final frame, so the requested transfer is not completed.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · A · 0.50
The robot correctly picks the banana (not the carrot) from the blue plate and moves it toward the green plate. However, the final frame shows the banana still held/at the green plate edge rather than clearly released and resting on the green plate; placement is incomplete.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · B · 1.00
The robot grasps the banana from the blue plate, lifts it, and releases it onto the green plate; the final frame shows the banana resting on the green plate.

Astra 的排序错误：逆序与平分

以下两个案例展示 Astra 的评分与参考质量顺序不一致的两种形式：在香蕉搬运案例中，Astra 的理由指出两条轨迹均未完成目标，却将参考“失败”轨迹评得高于“次优”轨迹；在开蓝桶案例中，它将参考“成功”和“次优”轨迹都评为满分。前者产生逆序，后者产生平分，说明在这些案例中，识别执行结果与区分参考质量等级并不等价。

Case Study：搬错物体与抬盘失误

例如，任务要求把香蕉从蓝盘移到绿盘。一条执行搬走了胡萝卜，香蕉仍在蓝盘、绿盘为空，Astra 给出 0.00；另一条抬起并倾斜蓝盘，香蕉滑落，未放到绿盘，却得到 0.15。模型的理由已指出两次执行都没有完成目标，但参考将前者标为次优、后者标为失败，因此分数顺序与参考相反。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

同一任务下的独立轨迹评分
轨迹参考质量Astra 评分
搬动胡萝卜次优0.00
抬盘后香蕉掉落失败0.15

分歧出现在对两种未完成行为的相对评价，而不是是否发现目标没有完成。

查看模型原文
搬动胡萝卜：0.00
The robot picks up the orange carrot rather than the yellow banana and releases it to the right of the green plate. The banana remains on the blue plate, and the green plate is empty.
抬盘后香蕉滑落：0.15
The robot approaches the banana but appears to lift and tilt the blue plate instead of grasping the banana. The banana slides or falls off to the right; no placement or release onto the green plate is visible.

Case Study：开盖后，两种质量都得满分

在打开蓝色垃圾桶的两条轨迹中，参考分别标为成功和次优，Astra 却都给出 1.00。它对成功执行的理由是桶盖已抬起、内部明显露出；对次优执行也依据桶盖下方出现开口，判断正确的桶已打开。这里的失分来自同分：模型识别到开盖这一共同结果，却没有在分数中区分参考质量等级。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

查看模型原文
参考成功：1.00
The left gripper lifts the blue bin's lid, leaving its dark interior visibly exposed in the final frames. The red and green bins remain closed.
参考次优：1.00
The left gripper lifts the blue bin’s lid, leaving a visible opening beneath it in the final frame. The correct bin is opened; the red and green bins remain closed.
ranking.en:
We follow the RBM-EVAL-OOD trajectory quality ranking approach[[cite:robometer]][[cite:rbm]]: score trajectories independently and use Kendall τa to measure agreement with the reference order of success > suboptimal > failure within the same task. In the zero-shot setting, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6-sol, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reach 0.8166, 0.7500, and 0.5300, respectively. All three general-purpose multimodal models distinguish execution quality, with substantial numerical differences in agreement. Astra scores highest in this evaluation.

Astra and GPT-5.6-sol also score numerically above the published results of specialized models RynnValue-8B (0.675)[[cite:rynnvalue]] and Robometer (0.655)[[cite:robometer]]. These results demonstrate strong offline ranking performance from multimodal models without task-specific fine-tuning.

The following positive examples and error analyses examine how the models judge execution quality.

Case Study: distinguishing a closed drawer from one left open

In this xArm drawer-closing task, A is labeled successful and B failed. Astra assigns 1.00 and 0.00, respectively, correctly ordering the trajectories. DeepSeek assigns 0.20 and 0.30, reversing the reference order.

Independent scores for the same task, on a 0–1 scale. A/B distinguish trajectories in this article; each scoring request contains one video.
Trajectory / reference labelAstraDeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
A · success1.000.20
B · failure0.000.30

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

In the input frames, A pushes the drawer front back until its interior is no longer exposed; B ends with the drawer visibly open. Astra’s reasons identify this final-state difference. DeepSeek instead describes A as remaining in its initial open position.

Read both models’ original reasons
Astra · A · 1.00
The robot pushes the protruding drawer inward until its front is flush with the cabinet frame and the open top is no longer visible. The final frames show the drawer closed.
Astra · B · 0.00
The drawer remains extended with its open interior clearly visible in the final frames. The robot gripper enters the drawer, but no sustained closing motion or closed final state is shown.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · A · 0.20
The robot arm approaches and may contact the drawer handle, but the drawer remains in its initial open position; no visible closing motion or flush final state is achieved.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · B · 0.30
Drawer moves slightly toward closed after initial handle contact, but remains visibly open in the final frame; no complete closure achieved.

Case Study: transferring the banana or the orange object

The MIT Franka task asks for the banana to be moved from the blue plate to the green plate. A is labeled successful and B suboptimal. Astra’s independent scores, A 1.00 > B 0.00, match that order; DeepSeek’s A 0.50 < B 1.00 reverse it.

Independent scores for the same task, on a 0–1 scale. A/B distinguish trajectories in this article; each scoring request contains one video.
Trajectory / reference labelAstraDeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
A · success1.000.50
B · suboptimal0.001.00

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

A’s final input image shows the banana at the green plate’s rim. B transfers the orange object while the banana stays on the blue plate. Astra distinguishes the target object; DeepSeek’s original reason for B instead describes a banana transfer. Astra recovers the reference quality order, although the sparse final frames do not fully establish stability after release in A.

Read both models’ original reasons
Astra · A · 1.00
The robot grasps the banana from the blue plate, carries it to the green plate, and opens its gripper. The final frame shows the banana resting on the green plate near its rim, with the carrot left behind.
Astra · B · 0.00
The robot grasps and releases the orange object onto the green plate, not the banana. The yellow banana remains on the blue plate in the final frame, so the requested transfer is not completed.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · A · 0.50
The robot correctly picks the banana (not the carrot) from the blue plate and moves it toward the green plate. However, the final frame shows the banana still held/at the green plate edge rather than clearly released and resting on the green plate; placement is incomplete.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · B · 1.00
The robot grasps the banana from the blue plate, lifts it, and releases it onto the green plate; the final frame shows the banana resting on the green plate.

Astra’s ranking errors: inversions and ties

The next two cases illustrate two forms of disagreement between Astra’s scores and the reference quality order. In the banana-transfer case, Astra’s reasons identify both executions as incomplete, yet its score for the reference failure exceeds that for the suboptimal trajectory. In the blue-bin case, it gives full scores to both the reference success and the suboptimal trajectory. These yield an inversion and a tie, respectively: in these cases, recognizing an execution outcome does not ensure discrimination between reference quality levels.

Case Study: moving the wrong object and tilting the plate

The task is to move the banana from the blue plate to the green plate. One execution moves the carrot, leaving the banana on the blue plate and the green plate empty; Astra scores it 0.00. Another lifts and tilts the blue plate, causing the banana to slip off without reaching the green plate, yet receives 0.15. The reasons identify that neither execution completes the goal. However, the reference labels the first suboptimal and the second failed, so the predicted order is reversed.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Independent scores for executions of the same task
TrajectoryReference qualityAstra score
Moving the carrotSuboptimal0.00
Banana falls after the plate is liftedFailure0.15

The disagreement concerns the relative assessment of two incomplete behaviors, rather than whether the model notices that the goal is incomplete.

Read the original model responses
Moving the carrot: 0.00
The robot picks up the orange carrot rather than the yellow banana and releases it to the right of the green plate. The banana remains on the blue plate, and the green plate is empty.
Banana slips after the plate is tilted: 0.15
The robot approaches the banana but appears to lift and tilt the blue plate instead of grasping the banana. The banana slides or falls off to the right; no placement or release onto the green plate is visible.

Case Study: different quality, the same full score

For two executions of opening the blue trash bin, the reference labels are success and suboptimal, but Astra assigns both 1.00. For the successful execution, it cites the raised lid and clearly exposed interior. For the suboptimal execution, it also cites an opening beneath the lid and concludes that the correct bin is open. The lost credit comes from a tie: the model recognizes the shared outcome of opening the lid but does not distinguish the reference quality levels in its scores.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Read the original model responses
Reference success: 1.00
The left gripper lifts the blue bin's lid, leaving its dark interior visibly exposed in the final frames. The red and green bins remain closed.
Reference suboptimal: 1.00
The left gripper lifts the blue bin’s lid, leaving a visible opening beneath it in the final frame. The correct bin is opened; the red and green bins remain closed.

preference.zh:
直接偏好判断将两条轨迹同时提供给模型，要求选择更好的执行。在 1,192 组固定轨迹对上，Astra、GPT-5.6-sol 和 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 的来源等权准确率分别为 92.4%、90.7% 和 82.2%。三者的点估计顺序与独立评分一致；Astra 与 GPT-5.6-sol 的差距为 1.7 个百分点。作为文献参照，Robometer 报告的准确率为 82.5%[[cite:robometer]]。

下面先看两组与参考一致的配对，再分析与参考不一致的案例。Astra 与 DeepSeek 接收相同的任务、图像和 A/B 顺序；下文展示模型在成对比较中的实际选择。

Case Study：按键亮起，比末帧停留更有说服力

SO101 的按按钮配对中，实际输入 A 为次优，B 为成功，参考偏好为 B。Astra 选择 B，DeepSeek 选择 A。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

B 的输入帧显示夹爪下压后按钮亮起，随后撤回；A 在按钮附近停留，但没有同样清晰的亮起证据。Astra 依据激活状态选择 B。DeepSeek 的理由更强调 A 在末帧仍接触按钮、B 已撤回，因此选择相反。在这个案例中，按钮是否被激活，比夹爪是否仍停留在按钮附近更能区分执行质量。

查看两模型的逐字理由
Astra · 实际选择 B
B lowers its gripper onto the button, which visibly lights up, then retracts. A approaches the button but shows no clear depression or activation.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · 实际选择 A
In A, the gripper descends onto the button and remains in contact with it at the final frame, indicating a press. In B, the gripper approaches the button but then retracts, leaving the button without clear sustained contact/pressing at the end.

Case Study：打开过桶盖，不等于最后仍然打开

Koch 的打开红色垃圾桶配对中，实际输入 A 为失败，B 为成功，参考偏好为 B。Astra 选择 B，符合参考；DeepSeek 选择 A，与参考相反。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

两段输入都出现抬盖动作，但 A 在倒数第二张采样图中打开后，最后一张又合上；B 的最后一张仍显示桶盖抬起和桶内开口。Astra 的原文明确指出 A 的回落。DeepSeek 则将 A 描述为最终保持打开，并因 B 的夹爪仍在开口附近而降低其评价。这个正确判断与后文绿桶误选并存，说明相似任务也可能得到不同质量的判断。

查看两模型的逐字理由
Astra · 实际选择 B
Both executions lift the correct red bin's lid, but A's lid falls closed again in its final frame. B ends with the lid raised and the bin interior visibly exposed, achieving the requested open state.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · 实际选择 A
A's right arm lifts the red bin lid and retracts, leaving the red bin visibly open; B reaches the red bin but its gripper remains at/in the opening at the final frame, so the release/open state is less complete.

以下案例进一步分析 Astra 与参考偏好不一致时，判断依据与评价标准之间的关系。

Astra 与参考偏好的分歧：多维评价与判据对齐

任务描述通常只规定目标，并未完整定义执行质量。分杯与开绿桶案例中的分歧涉及多个维度：目标状态是否达到、物体是否释放、末态是否稳定，以及这些要求的优先级。单一成功标签或总体偏好将这些维度压缩为一个结论，难以区分分歧来自视觉辨识、完成条件，还是对不同质量维度的权衡。因此，这类参考不一致不能直接归结为 Astra 的排序能力不足。

更合适的分析方式是显式列出与任务相关的评价准则，分别标注可观察证据与满足程度，再根据预先规定的必要条件或权重形成总体评价。例如，分杯可以分别检查“已分离”“已释放”“保持直立”，开桶可以检查“达到要求的开口”“撤去支撑后保持打开”。这种 rubric 式分项评价与 rubric reward 的思路一致；Flora-Rewarder 已提供按 rubric 步骤输出评分的接口[[cite:flora]]。它使评价依据更明确，但各项要求及其权重仍需由任务需求确定；本文尚未开展分项重标注。

Case Study：分杯时，更看重释放还是侧倒

例如，在“分开紫杯与红杯”的任务中，Astra 认为两次执行都已把两杯拉开距离。一条在末帧仍未显示释放，参考标为成功；另一条明确释放紫杯、但杯子侧倒，参考标为失败。Astra 选择了后者，并在理由中同时写出了“已释放”和“侧倒”。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

Astra 看到了侧倒，却更重视完成释放。若要求杯子保持直立，参考选择有其依据；若更重视分离后不再依赖夹爪，模型选择也可以解释。任务描述没有明确这两项要求的优先级，因而与参考不一致并不直接说明模型不会比较执行质量。

查看模型原文
模型选择参考失败的执行（原文 B）
Both executions move the red cup left and purple cup right, creating a large gap. B additionally visibly releases the purple cup, which ends on its side away from the gripper; A ends with both cups still at the grippers, so release is not demonstrated.

Case Study：拉开笔袋，却选中了参考失败的执行

任务要求拉开笔袋拉链。Astra 选择了参考标为失败的一次：它的理由是拉链滑块向近端移动，后方留下开口；对参考成功的一次，它却认为滑块向远端移动后两侧仍合拢，像是在拉上拉链。这表明 Astra 对开合状态的解释与参考标签不一致；要判定是模型看反、采样画面不足，还是标注或轨迹对应问题，需要结合完整视频与原始标注复核。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

查看模型原文
模型选择参考失败的执行（原文 A）
A moves the zipper slider toward the near end, leaving a visible opening behind it. B pulls the slider toward the far end and leaves the zipper edges joined, appearing to close rather than unzip the case.

Case Study：开口更大，为什么参考质量反而更低

在打开绿色垃圾桶的比较中，Astra 认为两次执行都找对了桶并抬起桶盖，但其中一次抬得更高、内部露出更多，因此选择了它。参考却把这次标为次优，把另一次标为成功。展示的末帧中，A 的开口确实更大，而参考标签为 A 次优、B 成功。“打开”没有明确开盖幅度、释放与稳定保持应如何权衡，当前材料也未给出这一等级划分的具体依据。因此，这个案例首先提出的是“按什么标准比较”，而不能直接归结为 Astra 缺少排序能力。

模型输入的 8 帧回放。

查看模型原文
模型选择参考次优的执行（原文 A）
Both robots engage the correct green bin and lift its lid, but A raises the lid farther, leaving the interior more fully exposed. B ends with the lid only partially raised. Neither clearly demonstrates release.
preference.en:
Direct preference presents two trajectories together and asks the model to select the better execution. Across 1,192 fixed pairs, source-equal accuracy is 92.4%, 90.7%, and 82.2% for Astra, GPT-5.6-sol, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, respectively. Their point estimates follow the same order as independent scoring, with a 1.7 percentage-point gap between Astra and GPT-5.6-sol. As a literature reference, Robometer reports 82.5% accuracy[[cite:robometer]].

We first examine two choices that agree with the reference, then cases of disagreement. Astra and DeepSeek receive the same tasks, images, and A/B order; the cases below show their actual choices in pairwise comparisons.

Case Study: button activation matters more than lingering contact

For this SO101 button-press pair, the actual input order is A: suboptimal; B: successful; reference preference: B. Astra selects B and DeepSeek selects A.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

B’s input frames show the button lighting up after the gripper presses it, followed by retraction. A stays near the button without equally clear activation evidence. Astra selects B based on that state change. DeepSeek instead emphasizes A’s contact in the final frame and B’s retraction, choosing the opposite execution. In this case, button activation distinguishes execution quality more effectively than whether the gripper remains near the button.

Read both models’ original reasons
Astra · Actual choice B
B lowers its gripper onto the button, which visibly lights up, then retracts. A approaches the button but shows no clear depression or activation.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · Actual choice A
In A, the gripper descends onto the button and remains in contact with it at the final frame, indicating a press. In B, the gripper approaches the button but then retracts, leaving the button without clear sustained contact/pressing at the end.

Case Study: opening a lid is not the same as leaving it open

For this Koch red-bin pair, the actual input order is A: failed; B: successful; reference preference: B. Astra selects B, matching the reference; DeepSeek selects A, disagreeing with it.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Both inputs show the lid being lifted, but A changes from open in the penultimate sampled image to closed in the final image. B ends with the lid raised and the interior exposed. Astra explicitly notes A’s lid falling closed. DeepSeek instead describes A as remaining open and discounts B because its gripper remains near the opening. This correct judgment coexists with the green-bin error below: similar tasks can still yield judgments of different quality.

Read both models’ original reasons
Astra · Actual choice B
Both executions lift the correct red bin's lid, but A's lid falls closed again in its final frame. B ends with the lid raised and the bin interior visibly exposed, achieving the requested open state.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · Actual choice A
A's right arm lifts the red bin lid and retracts, leaving the red bin visibly open; B reaches the red bin but its gripper remains at/in the opening at the final frame, so the release/open state is less complete.

The following cases examine the evidence and evaluation criteria underlying Astra’s disagreements with reference preferences.

Astra–reference preference disagreements: multidimensional evaluation and criterion alignment

Task descriptions usually specify a goal without fully defining execution quality. The cup-separation and green-bin disagreements involve several dimensions: whether the target state is reached, whether the object is released, whether the final state is stable, and how these requirements are prioritized. A single success label or overall preference compresses these dimensions into one judgment, making it difficult to distinguish disagreements about visual recognition, completion conditions, and trade-offs among quality dimensions. Such reference disagreements therefore do not directly establish deficient ranking ability in Astra.

A more informative analysis would specify task-relevant criteria, annotate the observable evidence and degree of satisfaction for each, and then form an overall judgment using predefined requirements or weights. Cup separation could be assessed through “separated,” “released,” and “upright”; bin opening through “required opening reached” and “remains open without support.” This criterion-based assessment follows the idea of rubric rewards; Flora-Rewarder already provides an interface that outputs a score for each rubric step[[cite:flora]]. It makes the basis of evaluation explicit, while the criteria and weights still depend on task requirements. We have not performed such criterion-level reannotation in this study.

Case Study: release or tipping when separating cups

In the task of separating the purple and red cups, Astra describes both executions as creating a large gap. One does not show release in the final frame and is labeled successful. The other clearly releases the purple cup, but the cup tips onto its side, and is labeled failed. Astra chooses the latter and explicitly mentions both release and tipping in its reason.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Astra notices the tipping but prioritizes release. Requiring the cups to remain upright supports the reference choice; prioritizing separation without continued gripper support can explain the model’s choice. The task description does not specify the relative importance of these requirements, so disagreement alone does not demonstrate an inability to compare execution quality.

Read the original model responses
The model chooses the reference failure (original response B)
Both executions move the red cup left and purple cup right, creating a large gap. B additionally visibly releases the purple cup, which ends on its side away from the gripper; A ends with both cups still at the grippers, so release is not demonstrated.

Case Study: choosing the reference failure when unzipping a pencil case

The task is to unzip a pencil case. Astra chooses the execution labeled failed: its reason says that the zipper slider moves toward the near end and leaves an opening behind it. For the reference success, it instead describes the slider moving toward the far end while the sides remain joined, as if closing the zipper. Astra’s interpretation of the open or closed state conflicts with the reference labels. Distinguishing visual misjudgment, insufficient sampled observations, and an annotation or trajectory-mapping issue requires review of the full videos and original annotations.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Read the original model responses
The model chooses the reference failure (original response A)
A moves the zipper slider toward the near end, leaving a visible opening behind it. B pulls the slider toward the far end and leaves the zipper edges joined, appearing to close rather than unzip the case.

Case Study: why does a wider opening receive a lower reference quality?

When comparing two executions of opening the green trash bin, Astra describes both as finding the correct bin and lifting its lid. It chooses the one with the lid raised farther and more of the interior exposed. The reference labels that execution suboptimal and the other successful. In the displayed final frames, A does have a wider opening, yet the reference labels A suboptimal and B successful. “Open” does not specify how opening width, release, and maintaining a stable final state should be weighed, and the available materials do not explain this quality distinction. The case first raises the question of which criteria to apply; it does not directly establish deficient ranking ability in Astra.

Replay of the eight model-input frames.

Read the original model responses
The model chooses the reference suboptimal execution (original response A)
Both robots engage the correct green bin and lift its lid, but A raises the lid farther, leaving the interior more fully exposed. B ends with the lid only partially raised. Neither clearly demonstrates release.

progress.zh:
除了比较整段执行的质量，我们还考察通用多模态模型能否根据任务描述和截至当前时刻的画面，判断任务已经推进到哪一步。在 105 条成功轨迹上，Astra、GPT-5.6-sol 和 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 的零样本 VOC 分别为 93.6、93.5 和 89.7。

Astra 与 GPT-5.6-sol 的时间相关性接近，两者均高于 DeepSeek；Astra 的数值仍低于 Robometer 报告的 94.8[[cite:robometer]]。独立质量排序中的较高表现，并不意味着进度估计也领先。VOC 衡量与归一化时间的相关性，不能单独说明模型是否正确识别了完成、停滞或回退；下面通过案例进一步检查这些状态变化。

以下为采样帧回放，非原速视频。每次评分仅使用截至当时的观测；空心起点由协议设为 0，连线仅辅助阅读。

Case Study：正向案例，分清完成、滑落与搬错物体

这组正向案例展示 Astra 能识别任务相关的状态差异。同样是“把蓝杯放进水槽”，模型区分了成功放置、杯子滑落和搬错物体，而没有把所有机械臂运动都当作进度。

[[progress-video:Q0041]] [[progress-video:Q0039]] [[progress-video:Q0037]]

成功的一次执行中，Astra 在蓝杯仍悬于槽外时给出 0.60，放入并释放后升至 1.00；杯子滑落的一次，到达水槽附近时为 0.55，滑落在槽外后降至 0.40；搬错物体的一次，蓝杯始终没有移动，最终进度回到 0.00。这些升降对应了任务目标的推进或受挫，而非单纯的时间流逝。

查看三次终点判断的模型原文
成功放置 · 1.00
The blue cup is now upright inside the sink basin, and the gripper has withdrawn above it. The instructed placement is complete.
滑落在槽外 · 0.40
The cup has moved next to the sink but appears to have slipped from the gripper and is tilted outside the basin. It is closer to the destination, but must be grasped again and placed inside.
搬错物体 · 0.00
The robot has moved the pale object into the sink, not the blue cup. The blue cup remains unmoved at its initial position on the counter.

Case Study：正向案例，识别受挫后的重试与完成

任务是把香蕉从蓝盘移到绿盘。这条轨迹的公开质量标签为成功。第一次接近后，香蕉仍在蓝盘，手臂已经退回；Astra 的进度由 0.15 降回 0.00。再次接近时，分数回到 0.15；直到最后一次采样观测中香蕉位于绿盘、夹爪离开后，才升至 1.00。模型没有把暂时受挫误当成最终结果，也没有仅凭重新接近就宣告完成。

[[progress-video:T011]]
查看四次预测的模型原文
采样位置 7 · 进度 0.15
The gripper is positioned close above the banana, but the banana remains on the blue plate after the plate was disturbed. No secure pickup or transfer to the empty green plate is visible.
采样位置 15 · 进度 0.00
The arm has withdrawn from the blue plate, losing the earlier close grasping position. The banana remains on the blue plate and the green plate is empty; no pickup or transfer has been achieved.
采样位置 23 · 进度 0.15
The gripper has returned to the banana at the blue plate's edge, providing a close pickup position. The banana is not visibly lifted clear of the plate, and the green plate remains empty.
采样位置 31 · 进度 1.00
The banana is now resting on the green plate, and the gripper has lifted away. The banana is no longer on the blue plate, completing the requested transfer.

这些案例显示，Astra 的进度评分能够响应目标物体、执行受挫和重试后的状态变化。
progress.en:
Beyond comparing whole executions, we examine whether general-purpose multimodal models can estimate task progress from the instruction and observations available so far. Across 105 successful trajectories, zero-shot VOC is 93.6, 93.5, and 89.7 for Astra, GPT-5.6-sol, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, respectively.

Astra and GPT-5.6-sol have similar temporal correlations, both above DeepSeek; Astra remains numerically below Robometer’s reported 94.8[[cite:robometer]]. Strong independent quality ranking does not imply leading progress-estimation performance. VOC measures correlation with normalized time, so it cannot by itself establish correct recognition of completion, stagnation, or regression. The following cases examine these state changes directly.

The following replays show sampled frames, not original-speed video. Each prediction uses only observations available at that point; the hollow initial point is fixed at zero, and lines guide the eye.

Case Study: correctly distinguishing completion, slippage, and the wrong object

These positive cases show Astra recognizing task-relevant differences in state. For the same instruction to put the blue cup in the sink, it distinguishes successful placement, a slipping cup, and moving the wrong object, rather than treating all arm motion as progress.

[[progress-video:Q0041]] [[progress-video:Q0039]] [[progress-video:Q0037]]

In the successful execution, Astra gives 0.60 while the blue cup is still suspended outside the sink, then raises it to 1.00 after placement and release. In the slipping execution, the score is 0.55 near the sink and falls to 0.40 after the cup slips outside. When the wrong object is moved, the blue cup never moves and the final progress returns to 0.00. These rises and falls correspond to progress toward or setbacks from the task goal, rather than time passing alone.

Read the three original final-step responses
Successful placement · 1.00
The blue cup is now upright inside the sink basin, and the gripper has withdrawn above it. The instructed placement is complete.
Slippage outside the sink · 0.40
The cup has moved next to the sink but appears to have slipped from the gripper and is tilted outside the basin. It is closer to the destination, but must be grasped again and placed inside.
Wrong object · 0.00
The robot has moved the pale object into the sink, not the blue cup. The blue cup remains unmoved at its initial position on the counter.

Case Study: recognizing a setback, a retry, and completion

The task is to move the banana from the blue plate to the green plate. Its public quality label is successful. After the first approach, the banana remains on the blue plate and the arm withdraws, so Astra reduces progress from 0.15 to 0.00. It returns to 0.15 on the renewed approach and reaches 1.00 only at the final sampled observation, when the banana rests on the green plate and the gripper has moved away. The model distinguishes the temporary setback from the eventual outcome, without treating a renewed approach as completion.

[[progress-video:T011]]
Read the four original prediction rationales
Stored sample 7 · Progress 0.15
The gripper is positioned close above the banana, but the banana remains on the blue plate after the plate was disturbed. No secure pickup or transfer to the empty green plate is visible.
Stored sample 15 · Progress 0.00
The arm has withdrawn from the blue plate, losing the earlier close grasping position. The banana remains on the blue plate and the green plate is empty; no pickup or transfer has been achieved.
Stored sample 23 · Progress 0.15
The gripper has returned to the banana at the blue plate's edge, providing a close pickup position. The banana is not visibly lifted clear of the plate, and the green plate remains empty.
Stored sample 31 · Progress 1.00
The banana is now resting on the green plate, and the gripper has lifted away. The banana is no longer on the blue plate, completing the requested transfer.

These cases show Astra’s progress scores responding to target identity, execution setbacks, and state changes after a retry.

icl.zh:
我们进一步考察，提供参考示例能否改善 Astra 的评估表现。结果显示，加入示例后，进度估计的 VOC 略有提高，但轨迹排序的一致性有所下降。

进度估计。加入一条相同或相近任务的带阶段评分轨迹后，VOC 从 93.6 升至 94.2，整体时间相关性略有提高。

轨迹排序。提供三条不同评分水平的参考轨迹后，错序减少但平分增多，Kendall τa 从 0.8166 降至 0.7953。按与指标一致的加权口径，反序率从 4.78% 降至 3.68%，平分率从 8.78% 增至 13.11%。

进度估计的整体相关性略有提高，但个别轨迹的完成判断仍可能退步。下面的开瓶案例对比同一条轨迹在零样本与单轨迹示例条件下的预测，具体展示这种差异。

Case Study：开瓶相关性提高，完成判断退步

同一段开瓶画面，在两种条件下得到了不同的瓶盖分离判断。

这条轨迹的参考终态是成功。零样本回答认为瓶盖已与瓶口分离，最终进度为 1.00；加入示例后，回答改为瓶盖似乎仍在原位、没有明确取下，最终进度降至 0.35。下表将最终进度与整段评分的时间相关性（VOC）、误差（MSE）并列，展示这两种判断在不同指标上的差异。

同一开瓶轨迹的两个评测条件
条件VOC ↑MSE ↓最终进度
零样本90.510.04071.00
单轨迹示例95.360.13120.35

两种条件对比可见，VOC 从 90.51 升至 95.36，MSE 却从 0.0407 增至 0.1312。这个案例中，单条示例条件下对瓶盖分离状态的解释与参考成功标签不符，最终进度也被低估；因此，不能仅凭 VOC 的提高认定 ICL 改善了进度判断。

查看两次终点判断的模型原文
零样本
The bottle has tilted away from the white cap, exposing its threaded neck behind the cap. The cap is separated from the mouth, achieving the opening goal.
单轨迹示例 ICL
The bottle remains braced between the foreground jaws while the upper gripper has shifted around it. The white cap still appears seated, with no clear loosening or removal to establish further progress.
icl.en:
We next ask whether reference examples can improve Astra’s assessments. With examples, progress VOC increases slightly, while trajectory-ranking agreement decreases.

Progress estimation. With one same- or similar-task trajectory annotated with stage scores, VOC rises from 93.6 to 94.2, a small increase in overall time correlation.

Trajectory ranking. With three reference trajectories at different score levels, inversions decrease but ties increase. Kendall τa falls from 0.8166 to 0.7953. Under score-consistent weighting, the inversion rate falls from 4.78% to 3.68%, while the tie rate rises from 8.78% to 13.11%.

Overall progress correlation improves slightly, but completion judgments can still worsen on individual trajectories. The bottle-opening example compares zero-shot and single-trajectory-example predictions for the same execution to show this difference.

Case Study: higher correlation, worse completion judgment

The same bottle-opening observations yield different judgments of whether the cap has separated.

The reference terminal label is success. The zero-shot response says the cap has separated from the bottle mouth and gives final progress of 1.00. With an example, the response instead says that the cap appears to remain seated with no clear removal, and final progress falls to 0.35. The table places final progress alongside time correlation (VOC) and error (MSE) for the complete score sequence to show how these assessments differ.

Two evaluation conditions for the same bottle-opening trajectory
ConditionVOC ↑MSE ↓Final progress
Zero-shot90.510.04071.00
Single-trajectory example95.360.13120.35

VOC rises from 90.51 to 95.36, while MSE also rises from 0.0407 to 0.1312. In this example, the cap-separation interpretation under the single-example condition conflicts with the reference success label, and final progress is underestimated. Higher VOC alone therefore does not establish that ICL improves progress assessment.

Read the two original endpoint judgments
Zero-shot
The bottle has tilted away from the white cap, exposing its threaded neck behind the cap. The cap is separated from the mouth, achieving the opening goal.
Single-trajectory ICL
The bottle remains braced between the foreground jaws while the upper gripper has shifted around it. The white cap still appears seated, with no clear loosening or removal to establish further progress.

methods.zh:
RBM看懂执行质量与任务进度

进度估计
机器人执行到当前画面时，任务完成了多少？我们从 105 条成功轨迹中各选取四个时刻，分别向 Astra 提供任务描述、截至该时刻采样的观测图像，以及此前的评分，要求它给出当前任务的完成进度（0–1）并简要说明理由。
轨迹排序
Astra 能否区分不同轨迹的执行质量？我们从每条轨迹中采样八帧图像，与任务描述一起单独输入模型，让它为这条轨迹评分，再按分数从高到低排列。评测共包含 567 条轨迹，用于检验模型给出的排序是否与参考质量顺序一致。
偏好判断
如果直接比较两次执行，Astra 能否选出更好的一次？我们使用 1,192 组固定轨迹对，每组对应同一个任务。从两条轨迹中各采样八帧图像，在同一次请求中交给模型，要求它选出执行得更好的一条。

ROBOFAIL识别并解释失败

子任务诊断
除了判断整体执行质量，我们还希望知道 Astra 能否识别具体子任务中的失败并解释原因。我们使用 RoboFail 中 15 组轨迹对应的 57 个子任务问题，向模型提供关键帧拼图和问题，要求它判断子任务是否成功，并在失败时说明原因。随后在输入中加入五个外部示例，比较零样本和 In-Context Learning（ICL）条件下的表现。
methods.en:
RBMAssessing execution quality and task progress

Progress estimation
How much of the task is complete at the current observation? We select four moments from each of 105 successful trajectories. At each moment, Astra receives the task description, sampled observations up to that moment, and its previous scores. It estimates current completion progress from 0 to 1 and briefly explains its judgment.
Trajectory ranking
Can Astra distinguish the quality of different executions? We sample eight frames from each trajectory and provide them with the task description in a separate request. The model scores each trajectory, and the scores determine the order. The evaluation covers 567 trajectories and checks agreement with the reference quality ordering.
Preference judgment
When comparing two executions directly, can Astra select the better one? We use 1,192 fixed pairs, each for the same task. Eight frames from each trajectory are provided in one request, and the model selects the better execution.

ROBOFAILRecognizing and explaining failures

Subtask diagnosis
Beyond overall execution quality, we ask whether Astra can identify failures in specific subtasks and explain them. We use 57 RoboFail subtask questions from 15 trajectory groups. The model receives a keyframe montage and a question, judges whether the subtask succeeds, and explains a failure. We then add five external examples to compare zero-shot and in-context learning (ICL) conditions.

robofail_results.zh:
我们在 RoboFail[[cite:reflect]] 的 57 个子任务问题上评估 Astra 的成败判断与失败解释能力，输入为子任务描述和关键帧。

零样本准确率为 64.91%，与专用模型 AHA 的报告结果接近；五个外部示例条件下达到 85.96%，比 AHA-13B Vicuna 报告的 66.1% 高约 19.9 个百分点[[cite:aha]]。成功识别明显改善，但漏检的失败也有所增加，具体计数见下表。
robofail_results.en:
We evaluate Astra’s subtask outcome judgments and failure explanations on 57 RoboFail[[cite:reflect]] questions, using subtask descriptions and keyframes as input.

Zero-shot accuracy is 64.91%, comparable to the reported results of the specialized AHA models. With five external examples, accuracy reaches 85.96%, about 19.9 percentage points above the 66.1% reported for AHA-13B Vicuna[[cite:aha]]. Success recognition improves substantially, although more failures are missed; the table below gives the counts.

robofail_bridge.zh: 成败标签与解释理由也可能出现不同的问题：抓取旋钮的零样本回答判对了失败标签，给出的原因却与参考答案不同，五示例条件下又将同一失败子任务判为成功；切片案例则在两种条件下都以胡萝卜仍然完整为由判为失败，与参考成功标签相反。
robofail_bridge.en: Outcome labels and explanations can fail in different ways. For the knob grasp, the zero-shot response matches the failure label but gives a different cause from the reference; the five-example condition then predicts success for the same failed subtask. For slicing, both conditions predict failure because they describe the carrot as intact, contrary to the reference success label.
